title: Billing Office Policy on Claims, Remittances and Secondary Coverage for the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program
content:
Every refill shipped on a payer tier of the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is billed to the payer named by the program's coverage record by one original claim per shipment, with the ship date as the date of service; the self-pay tier files no claims.

## Billing office policy

**Timely filing.** An original claim must be transmitted no later than the tier's timely filing limit in calendar days after the date of service of the shipment it bills, counted in calendar days from that ship date with the last day allowed; a shipment whose filing limit has passed is billed to neither the payer nor the customer and is written off by Larkfield.

**Corrected and void claims.** A corrected claim replaces an original claim when the units, item or dates billed were wrong or some of the units were returned, and a void claim withdraws an original claim when all of its units were returned; both reference the same shipment as the original.

**Patient responsibility on a remittance.** When a remittance posts, the patient responsibility added to the customer's balance is the allowed amount less the amount the payer paid, which the remittance itemizes as deductible, coinsurance and copay; Larkfield never posts more than that and never bills the customer the difference between its billed charge and the allowed amount on a payer tier.

**Secondary coverage.** On tiers where crossover to secondary applies and the customer has an in-effect secondary coverage record, the patient responsibility is crossed over to the secondary payer, and the secondary payer's payment is posted as a balance adjustment with reason secondary payer payment against that remittance before any amount is statemented; on other tiers a secondary coverage is billed by Larkfield's billing team only after the primary remittance posts.

**Medicaid.** On the Medicaid tier a customer is never billed for a Medicaid-covered item beyond the patient responsibility the Medicaid remittance shows.

## Remittance posting, worked through (hypothetical remittance)

| Line of the remittance | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|
| Larkfield billed charge | 310.00 |
| Allowed amount | 240.00 |
| Payer paid | 192.00 |
| Patient responsibility posted to the balance: allowed amount less payer paid | 48.00 |
| Difference between billed charge and allowed amount | 70.00 — never billed to the customer on a payer tier |

The 48.00 is the whole of what posts; the remittance itemizes it as deductible, coinsurance and copay.

## Filing limit, both sides (hypothetical figures)

With a filing limit of 365 calendar days and a ship date of 2026-02-10, an original claim transmitted on 2027-02-10 is within the limit (day 365, the last day allowed); a claim not transmitted by then is billed to neither the payer nor the customer and is written off by Larkfield.

## Points of judgement

- *The customer has an in-effect secondary coverage on a tier where crossover does not apply.* The secondary coverage is billed by Larkfield's billing team only after the primary remittance posts.
- *Some units of a payer-billed shipment were returned.* The original claim is replaced by a corrected claim referencing the same shipment; if all units were returned, a void claim withdraws it.
